stem: In which chemical reaction does carbon exibit variation of oxidation state from \(-4\) to \(+4\) ? Write balanced chemical reaction.
In which reaction does nitrogen exhibit variation of oxidation state from \(-3\) to \(+5\) ?

Calculate the oxidation number of underlined atoms.

a. \(\mathrm{H_2\underline{S}O_4}\)

b. \(\mathrm{H\underline{N}O_3}\)

c. \(\mathrm{H_3\underline{P}O_3}\)

d. \(\mathrm{K_2\underline{C}_2O_4}\)

e. \(\mathrm{H_2\underline{S}_4O_6}\)

f. \(\underline{\mathrm{Cr}}_2\mathrm{O_7^{2-}}\)

g. \(\mathrm{NaH_2\underline{P}O_4}\)

Justify that the following reactions are redox reaction; identify the species oxidized/reduced, which acts as an oxidant and which act as a reductant.

a. \(\mathrm{2Cu_2O(s) + Cu_2S(s) \longrightarrow 6Cu(s) + SO_2(g)}\)

b. \(\mathrm{HF(aq) + OH^{\ominus}(aq) \longrightarrow H_2O}(l) + \mathrm{F^{\ominus}(aq)}\)

c. \(\mathrm{I_2(aq) + 2S_2O_3^{2\ominus}(aq) \longrightarrow S_4O_6^{2\ominus}(aq) + 2I^{\ominus}(aq)}\)
_note: The three reactions are printed full-width beneath the item, running into the left margin of p-11; they belong to item D.

stem:
What is oxidation? Which one of the following pairs of species is in its oxidized state ?

a. \(\mathrm{Mg / Mg^{2\oplus}}\)

b. \(\mathrm{Cu / Cu^{2\oplus}}\)

c. \(\mathrm{O_2 / O^{2\ominus}}\)

d. \(\mathrm{Cl_2 / Cl^{\ominus}}\)

Justify the following reaction as redox reaction.

\(\mathrm{2Na(s) + S(s) \longrightarrow Na_2S(s)}\)

Find out the oxidizing and reducing agents.
Provide the stock notation for the following compounds : \(\mathrm{HAuCl_4}\), \(\mathrm{Tl_2O}\), \(\mathrm{FeO}\), \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\), \(\mathrm{MnO}\) and \(\mathrm{CuO}\).

Assign oxidation number to each atom in the following species.

a. \(\mathrm{Cr(OH)_4^{\ominus}}\)

b. \(\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3}\)

c. \(\mathrm{H_3BO_3}\)

Which of the following redox couple is stronger oxidizing agent ?

a. \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\) \((\mathrm{E^0} = 1.36\ \mathrm{V})\) and \(\mathrm{Br_2}\) \((\mathrm{E^0} = 1.09\ \mathrm{V})\)

b. \(\mathrm{MnO_4^{\ominus}}\) \((\mathrm{E^0} = 1.51\ \mathrm{V})\) and \(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2\ominus}}\) \((\mathrm{E^0} = 1.33\ \mathrm{V})\)
_note: The parenthesised E0 values are DATA SUPPLIED IN THE STEM, not a printed answer — they are not a `bookAnswer`.

stem:
Balance the following reactions by oxidation number method

a. \(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2\ominus}(aq) + SO_3^{2\ominus}(aq) \longrightarrow Cr^{3\oplus}(aq) + SO_4^{2\ominus}(aq)}\) (acidic)

b. \(\mathrm{MnO_4^{\ominus}(aq) + Br^{\ominus}(aq) \longrightarrow MnO_2(s) + BrO_3^{\ominus}(aq)}\) (basic)

c. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4(aq) + C(s) \longrightarrow CO_2(g) + SO_2(g) + H_2O}(l)\) (acidic)

d. \(\mathrm{Bi(OH)_3(g) + Sn(OH)_3^{\ominus}(aq) \longrightarrow Bi(s) + Sn(OH)_6^{2\ominus}(aq)}\) (basic)
_note: ⚠ Sub-item d is printed with the state symbol `(g)` on Bi(OH)3, a solid hydroxide — the same species is correctly printed `(s)` in Q.4 B b on the same page. Transcribed as printed; an errata bracket is carried on the solution.
